survivingClaim: Precise obstruction holds. Rank Gamma_- is lower semicontinuous under bounded weak-* convergence (proved). In the self-dual conductor normalisation every Lee-Yang stage symbol is inner and tends to -1 on Re z > 0 for zeta phases and every unimodular twist (proved relative to the refereed stage theorem; measured), so the semicontinuity chain carries no information. With gamma factor and pole renormalisation the stage symbol has one right-half-plane pole per stage zero, identical for zeta, U and random twists (measured, argument-principle counts; not proved for all P). In the strip topology, zeta is zero-free in Re s > theta iff the pole-renormalised Euler stages are locally bounded on {Re s > theta, s != 1} (proved: Hurwitz + von Koch; no novelty). The Lee-Yang inequality gives a stage bound with exponent of order P, weaker than the trivial bound (proved up to an unjustified constant). No statement about zeros of zeta is established; R4 is not supplied.
obstruction: Rank Gamma_- is lower semicontinuous under bounded weak-* convergence, but in the self-dual conductor normalisation every stage symbol tends to the constant -1 on Re z > 0 for zeta and every unimodular twist, so the chain carries no information. With gamma factor and pole renormalisation the stage has one right-half-plane pole per stage zero (measured), liminf rank infinite. In the strip topology the limit step is Hurwitz plus local boundedness of pole-renormalised Euler stages, which is equivalent to the zero-free statement (von Koch). The Lee-Yang inequality gives a stage bound weaker than the trivial one.
controlsThatDefeat: unimodular twist U (same stage behaviour; fails only at the open step)
random unimodular twists (same pole counts, measured)
lesson: The Lee-Yang stage's index 0 is the inequality Re D_M'/D_M > -(log M)/2, which becomes empty as M grows; the conductor factor that makes stages self-dual erases the limit (symbol -> -1). Any limit step from zero-free product stages is Hurwitz plus local boundedness of pole-renormalised stages, which is RH restated as the PNT error term. r1 holds only at stage level (zero-free stages need the Euler product); the U control fails at the open step, not at a proved one. Primes up to 47 cannot show the convergence mode: the pole factor is within 15 percent of 1 there.
